schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: THE HOLDER OF THE PRE-BUILD MACHINES, and for now that is ALL it is. Akien's eight-step method — orient, constrain, survey, decompose, triage, hypothesize, validate, then build — names seven stages before a line of code is written, and each of the seven is a machine. This device owns them: they berth at cairn/devices/builder/machines/<stage>/, the nesting CLAUDE.md has always granted a device ("a device's held tools and machines nest under it at the same shape") and which nothing on disk had used until 2026-08-13. WHAT IS NOT HERE, DELIBERATELY: there is no builder process, no BaseDevice subclass, no probes, no instance in the rack. The folder exists so the parts have their owner, not because the owner runs. Akien, verbatim: "even tho we are not building a builder right now, if you want you can create a folder for it and have it own all the machine pieces. that makes sense." The parts are reachable and unchanged — /chart still calls all seven; the skill CALLS, this device HOLDS, and those are two relations, not one.
why: The lived symptom is the one Akien names at step 3: "Easy to skip; expensive when skipped." A pre-build stage that nobody owns is a stage that gets skipped, and the record of a skipped stage is a build that looks fine and is wrong about what it was for. The seven were loose at cairn/machines/ after the chart decomposition, which was correct as far as it went — it got them out from under a skill that must not hold them — but it left them ownerless in the middle of the rung, seven siblings of build_inspector and ruling with nothing on disk saying they are one thing. Law 6 is the answer: everything has exactly one owner. Naming the owner is what makes "the pre-build steps" a countable set rather than a phrase in a docstring, and it is what gives the eventual builder somewhere to already be.
invoke: not invoked — a holder, not a process. Its parts are imported: cairn.devices.builder.machines.<stage>.<stage>
entry: Born 2026-08-13 from Akien's enumeration of the eight-step method and the ruling that followed it (CairnCommons/decisions/2026-08-13-the-builder-device-holds-the-prebuild-machines.json). The seven stages arrived by git mv from cairn/machines/<stage>/, whole — charters, proofs and validations moved with the code, which is Law 5 holding through a relocation: intent, voyage and proofs kept their shared address by moving together.
state_and_history: NONE, and that is the measurement rather than an omission. This device holds no durable state of its own — it is a namespace with an owner. Each held machine keeps its own; the voyages that built the seven stages are recorded in the chart machine's history, which stayed whole with the skill (a record of truth is never split, Law 7). When the builder becomes a process, state.json and history.json arrive with it and this field is rewritten by that ticket, not before.
gates: no gate of its own yet. The gates that matter to the pre-build chain live at the stages (each stage's validate_* door) and at the emit chokepoint (cairn/tools/base/transitions.py: a cast ticket may not cross into BUILDME unless a berthed validate packet claims it — buildme_rides_the_chart). Naming that here rather than claiming a gate: this device gates nothing today.
falsifier: RED on any of: (1) a held stage reachable at cairn/machines/<stage>/ again — the loose berth growing back; (2) the roster, the derivation gate or any judge failing to see a held machine, which is the quiet failure the nesting descent was built against (address.component_dirs must descend a holder's own rungs, and cairn/tools/base/proofs/ pins it); (3) this device acquiring code that RUNS while this charter still says it does not; (4) a held stage importing a sibling stage — the coupling the 2026-08-13 decomposition removed, which each stage's own allowlist tooth pins; (5) a machine berthing here that is not a pre-build stage, which would make "builder" a junk drawer rather than an owner.
horizon: re-read when the builder becomes a process (it gets an instance, a rack berth, state and history), or when the stage list changes — Akien's step 8 note says building reveals hidden sub-problems that re-enter at step 4, so the loop's shape is expected to grow, and the roster of stages is OPEN by intention.
how_it_learns: IT DOES NOT, and the reason is that it has nothing to learn about: it holds, it does not decide. Every learning in the pre-build chain happens one rung down, inside a held stage — each is a question nexus with three strata (deterministic floor -> tree walk -> INFERENCE CEILING) that deposits its ceiling answers back into its own tree, so the stratum boundary moves down over time. THE CEILING IS HEX, NOT CLAUDE (ruling 2026-08-14-the-preamble-compiles-to-learn-not-to-be-cheap): the preamble's uncompiled remainder fails over to the M1 Studio at hex.local, and every failover DEPOSITS tree nodes, which is the mechanism by which the rung below fills. Claude's place in this is not the ceiling but the BUILD, and that is what makes Claude the ground truth rather than the tenant being evicted — 'and you'll still be doing the builds'. Nothing here is about token cost; Claude is cached. The honesty instrument over all seven is skills/chart/dial.py. When this device grows a process, that process will have to answer this question for itself and "it doesn't" will stop being valid.
traces_to: Law 1 (the pre-build preamble compiled; the resolver spent on the novel)
Law 4 (the holder is on disk, not a phrase in a docstring — and the census descends to find it)
Law 5 (intent, voyage and proofs moved together, keeping their shared address)
Law 6 (everything has exactly one owner; seven ownerless machines had none)
Law 9 (this charter says out loud what is NOT built, so nothing here reads green by silence)
owner: CC owns this folder's shape and the moves that fill it. Akien owns the eight-step method it is named for, and the ruling that made it a device.
proof: no proof of its own — there is no behaviour here to prove. The two claims this charter makes that CAN be measured are held elsewhere by design: that the census sees a held machine is pinned in cairn/tools/base/proofs/, and that each stage still works after the move is pinned by the stage's own proof, which moved with it. A proof asserting that an empty folder is empty is the hollow kind Law 8 refuses.
provenance: Akien, 2026-08-13, enumerating the method and then ruling on it: "those before build are the pre-build steps. eventually each will be it's own machine, and there will be a builder device class who has all of those reusable parts, moved to live inside of it. in fact, even tho we are not building a builder right now, if you want you can create a folder for it and have it own all the machine pieces. that makes sense."
